pages.text: $(bold)Description:$() The Observer Core sits on the central pedestal of the Throne. It is the remains of the previous observer and the socket of the observer array. It has been lit the whole time; it is only that no one has been connected to it.

$(bold)Installation procedure:$()$(br2)$(li)1. Complete an OBSR-3;$(br)$(li)2. hold that model and right-click the Observer Core to open the core interface;$(br)$(li)3. choose "Install Candidate Observer".$(br2)Installation consumes the model.

$(bold)Effect:$() after installation the core begins to refocus, which takes a short time.$(br2)On completion:$(br)$(li)the core lights;$(br)$(li)the array accepts a new observer;$(br)$(li)defocus terminates.$(br2)Blocks no longer drift, creatures are no longer replaced, and the weather no longer mutates.

$(bold)Aftermath:$() Termination is not repair. What has already drifted will not come back. The world will stop in the state it was in at the moment you completed it, but anything that escaped the gaze of the unfinished Observer has a chance to recover.

$(italic)The last thing that happened in the previous iteration was this:$(br2)its final two executors each had a line to pull. Neither line was within their stabilisation parameters.$(br2)Both of them knew they would not see the dawn.$()
$(italic)So they succeeded?$()$(br2)$(italic)Yes. The Observer is now entirely under the Foundation's control.$()$(br2)$(italic)Can they resist the temptation?$()$(br2)$(italic)Historically, no.$()
